Text:
A few months ago I cleared my calendar and started asking what I actually wanted my life to look like. This is some of what I found.

More soon. I'm glad you're here.

What makes you happy? Not the big things. The small, specific, ordinary things that don't cost anything and no one thinks to mention.

Mine are: the sound of a kettle. Books with broken spines. Mornings before anyone else wakes up. Letters that arrive by hand.

Tell me one of yours. I'm genuinely asking.

My wish for you today is small and very real. That something beautiful found you. That you felt, for one moment, exactly where you needed to be.

Sometimes I think that's all we're really doing — trying to be present long enough to notice the good things before they pass.

What are you wishing for someone today?

We poured everything into it. Three years, every penny, every ounce of effort.

And it hurt deeply to let it go.

Part 2 on Saturday.

"Forever is composed of nows." — Emily Dickinson

A slow morning. The kettle. The stillness before the day has opinions. I used to think productive mornings were the goal. Now I think present ones are.

She changed my life.

As a mom, being outside is how she refills. It started with a podcast — 1,000 Hours Outside — and then it was a friendship she never saw coming.

When that friend moved away, it hurt. But before she left, she introduced her to something.

An outdoor adventure school. Five hours in nature. All the parents, gathered together.

And what they found there...

Part 4 tomorrow.

What they found there — standing in that mountain school, surrounded by parents and kids just figuring it out together — was a gap.

A gap in knowledge. A gap in confidence. A gap in community for mamas who want to get outside with their kids and have no idea where to start.

She was there not that long ago. And now she wants to help fill it. She'll share as she learns.

Welcome. She is so glad you're here.

"It is the small everyday deed of ordinary folks that keep the darkness at bay. Small acts of kindness and love."
(Often attributed to Tolkien — whatever the source, I find it true.)

I keep thinking about this. The small deeds. The letters written. The meals made quietly. The phone calls returned. The ordinary acts of love that no one photographs or applauds.

Those are the things that hold everything together.

I've been working on something for a long time. I want to tell you about it.

It's called Moss & Mail — a monthly letter subscription club. Every month I write you a letter by hand, sealed with wax. Inside: seeds, a recipe card, original art, a tea bag, a photo from the mountains, a nature prompt, a Spotify playlist, and a postcard with a stamp already on it so you can send it to someone you love.

For people who still believe in the magic of opening a real envelope.
